t: Founded by William the Pious in 893, the duchy was ruled from Poitiers by the counts of Poitou for nearly two centuries.
Duke William IX is the earliest troubadour whose songs survive, and the ducal courts helped create courtly love poetry.
Through Eleanor of Aquitaine it passed to the English crown, which held Gascony until the French victory at Castillon in 1453.
dyk: William the Pious, the first duke of Aquitaine, founded the abbey of Cluny in 910; its reformed monasticism spread to hundreds of houses across Latin Europe.
ev: William the Pious, count of Auvergne, takes the title of duke of Aquitaine
William the Pious founds the abbey of Cluny
Eleanor of Aquitaine inherits the duchy and marries the future Louis VII of France
Eleanor marries Henry Plantagenet, joining Aquitaine to the Angevin lands
The Treaty of Paris confirms English rule of Gascony under French overlordship
Philip VI confiscates Gascony, opening the Hundred Years' War
The Treaty of Brétigny grants England an enlarged Aquitaine in full sovereignty
French victory at Castillon ends English rule; Guyenne joins France
